overview_raw: Delivery: online. See details . About this program The Applied Mass Timber Engineering (AMTE) Microcredential is an applied online training program co-developed by BCIT and Aspect Structural Engineers, designed to upskill structural engineers in the design of mass timber structures. The program equips practicing engineers and design professionals with the technical competencies needed to design gravity and lateral mass timber structural systems, develop advanced connection details, and apply real-world knowledge of fabrication, installation, and constructability. Courses are delivered fully online and are self-paced, making the program accessible to learners across British Columbia and Canada. The curriculum is built around an overarching exemplar project that threads through all four courses, exposing students to the broader design process as it unfolds in practice. Competencies are aligned with the National Building Code of Canada (NBCC) 2020 and relevant CSA standards. An optional 5-day in-person experiential learning course, TMBR 3550 – Advanced Mass Timber Construction for Engineers, is available to students who have successfully completed all four courses. This badged course is a separate offering and is not required to earn the microcredential. Who it’s for This microcredential is suited for structural engineers seeking to upskill, engineers-in-training who have recently entered the workforce, and new hires at mass timber design firms looking for a practical onboarding and training program. Study permit: International applicants accepted into this program are not eligible for a study permit. Apply to program Formal application to the microcredential is not required. Upon successful completion of the courses , email the program contact with your full name, student number, and mailing address to be issued a microcredential. courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course establishes the foundational knowledge required for participants to engage confidently in the Applied Mass Timber Engineering Microcredential. Through a progression from core terminology and product families to historical and regulatory context, to the technical properties of wood, participants develop a shared vocabulary and broad understanding of how mass timber performs, how it is procured and assembled, and how it fits within modern industrialized construction workflows. Participants also gain a clear understanding of MT's value proposition, typical project delivery workflows, and the code and regulatory framework governing mass timber construction in Canada primarily, and the United States. The course is delivered online with live sessions and prepares participants to enter the advanced engineering design courses that follow.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Gravity Design of Mass Timber Structures
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course develops participants' ability to design mass timber gravity systems through a structured, applied approach centred on a real exemplar project. Beginning with an analysis of an architectural scheme and project constraints, participants progress through the design of key gravity elements including beams, columns, one-way and two-way floor panels, and wall panels, with fire design integrated throughout. Emphasis is placed on understanding load paths, panelization options, and the practical implications of material selection and fabrication on design decisions. Design examples follow Canadian engineering practice and are aligned with NBCC 2020 and CSA O86 standards, with cross-validation using industry software.​ Prerequisite(s): 60% in TMBR 3510

courses.course_name: Lateral Force Resisting System (LFRS) Design in Mass Timber Structures
courses.prerequisite_raw: 60% in TMBR 3510 and 60% in TMBR 3520 and 60% in TMBR 3540
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Building on the structural arrangement established in the gravity systems course, this course develops participants' understanding of lateral load resistance in mass timber buildings. The course focuses primarily on mass timber diaphragm design in hybrid with steel or concrete vertical lateral force resisting systems, reflecting current practice. Participants work through the design of diaphragm components, panel connections, and interface details, with an emphasis on load path clarity, stiffness assumptions, and the constructability considerations that influence lateral system design. All-timber LFRS typologies are introduced and their limitations discussed. Design examples are aligned with NBCC 2020 and CSA O86.​ Prerequisite(s): 60% in TMBR 3510 and 60% in TMBR 3520 and 60% in TMBR 3540

courses.course_name: Advanced Topics in Mass Timber Connections
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course provides participants with a comprehensive understanding of mass timber connection design, from first principles through to the specification of proprietary systems. Drawing from the gravity systems key plan developed in the preceding course, participants explore connection arrangements at key structural interfaces and work through design examples for bolt and dowel type connections and self-tapping screws to CSA O86. Emphasis is placed on the role of manufacturers, fabrication tolerances, fire design requirements, and the practical realities of connection accessibility and assembly sequencing. The course equips participants to coordinate effectively between engineering design, shop drawings, and proprietary product technical reports.​ Prerequisite(s): 60% in TMBR 3510 and 60% in TMBR 3520
